title: Thursday · The Secret Path, Orange Shirt Day art & learning online
arrival: Bring your library book. We will learn through a story and art this morning, then use laptops after lunch. There is no school tomorrow.
note: Fire drill about 9:00; library 9:20–9:35. Coordinate with librarian if drill runs late. The Secret Path is approximately 60 minutes in full; select a coherent opening segment at a chapter boundary for 9:35–10:35, allowing introduction, snack and debrief. Teacher preview required for exact player, language, captions, sound, school access and stop point. Official screening page: https://downiewenjack.ca/sp-screening-guide/ ; official-linked player: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gj5GVJrImdE . Chanie Wenjack's story is distinct from Phyllis Webstad's Orange Shirt Day account. Art resource: ./activities/orange-shirt-art.html . Accessible companion: ./printables/belonging/Truth_and_Reconciliation_Companion.pdf . Teacher run sheet: docs/THURSDAY_2026-09-24.md. Keep credentials and individual support records out of this site.

blocks.title: Arrival, attendance & check-in
blocks.notes: Attendance first; collect outstanding forms and library books afterward.
studentSteps: Settle in and answer attendance.
Have your library book ready; hand in forms after attendance.

blocks.title: Prepare for the fire drill
blocks.notes: Review the actual route, meeting place and accessible exit arrangements without displaying a class list.
studentSteps: Listen for the signal and follow our practised route.
Walk calmly and stay with the class at our meeting place.

blocks.title: Fire drill & return
blocks.notes: Approximate timing; coordinate library arrival if delayed.
studentSteps: Practise a calm, safe response.
Return and get ready for library.

blocks.title: Library
blocks.notes: Established Thursday library time; adjust with librarian if drill runs late.
studentSteps: Return or renew your book and choose a new one.

blocks.title: The Secret Path · learn, listen & reflect
blocks.notes: 5-minute historical context and content choice; teacher-previewed opening segment of up to about 35–40 minutes, stopping at a natural chapter boundary by roughly 10:20; snack and short debrief by 10:35. Record exact stop for later continuation. Quiet-break and nonverbal responses are welcome. The official-linked player has not been playback-checked here.
studentSteps: Learn who Chanie Wenjack was and listen to an artistic retelling of his story.
Notice one detail and one choice of image, colour, word or sound.
You may share a thought, draw, point, or reflect quietly. Have snack near the end.

blocks.title: Orange Shirt Day art · begin our design
blocks.notes: Reconnect to the film, then distinctly revisit Phyllis Webstad's account. Show the existing art examples; 10:50–11:00 launch/model, 11:00–11:40 protected making, 11:40–11:45 explain a choice, 11:45–11:50 label/store/tidy. Everyone participates regardless of unfinished booklets. Plain paper is fine if paper-shirt templates are unavailable. Continue unfinished art later.
studentSteps: What do we want people to understand and remember through our artwork?
Choose a symbol and a short message connected to our learning. Draw, point, dictate or use supported writing.
Tell someone why you made one choice. Label and safely store your work before lunch.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.notes: Usual outside-play, transition and eating routine.
studentSteps: Follow our usual lunch routine.

blocks.title: Laptops · get started
blocks.notes: Collect devices; demonstrate intended Matific activity and how to ask for help. Do not project passwords.
studentSteps: Collect a laptop and sign in quietly.
Ask for help without sharing your password aloud.

blocks.title: Matific · first practice session
blocks.notes: All registered; first actual use still to be checked. Select practice and challenge appropriate to students; do not mark rounding/comparing as taught. Resolve quick access issues privately; record complex cases elsewhere for follow-up.
studentSteps: Try the assigned maths activities and explain a strategy.
Choose a challenge if you are ready; ask quietly for access help.

blocks.title: Movement & screen break
blocks.notes: Offer seated and standing movement choices; no one needs to leave an accessible position to participate.
studentSteps: Pause your screen, stretch or move in a way that works for you, and reset.

blocks.title: SpacesEDU · show & explain learning
blocks.notes: Model activity-only versus learning reflection. A work-in-progress photo and short text or audio can explain an artistic choice and connection to attributed learning. Check access individually; prepare the same reflection offline if unavailable. No public emotional disclosure.
studentSteps: Look at a model: ‘I chose ___ to show ___. This connects to our learning because ___.’
Share a photo of work in progress if practical, or explain by voice or writing. A supported response is welcome.
Add one next step: ‘My next step is ___.’ If access is not ready, prepare the reflection on paper.

blocks.title: Blooket review · if ready
blocks.notes: Optional teacher-reviewed set on taught material only. Otherwise continue posts or Matific; protect device return.
studentSteps: Join the reviewed class game if we have time.
Otherwise finish your post or continue Matific.

blocks.title: Return laptops, jobs & pack up
blocks.notes: Count devices, sign out, plug in, complete planners and jobs; remind students Friday is non-instructional.
studentSteps: Save, sign out and return your laptop to the correct slot.
Complete jobs, planners and pack-up. No school Friday.

backups: Carry forward the formal rounding and comparing decimals lesson; Wednesday's work block did not teach it.
Carry forward Nevermoor listening and the journal launch with a model.
Continue unfinished Orange Shirt Day artwork later without taking the computer block.
Discovery and reconciliation booklet completion remain separate; they do not gate shared art learning.
Continue the remaining Secret Path chapters after teacher preview; do not imply the full film was watched today.
Friday, September 25: non-instructional day. Monday, September 28: Reconciliation Walk at 9:30 am.
